title: Horns, Tongues and Teeth! Animal Heads for Kids
description:
Who has two horns on its nose? Who has a tongue as long as twenty inches? Pick your answer with Milo the bluebird, then find out: a rhino's two horns keep growing all its life, a giraffe grabs leaves with its long tongue and chews its cud, and a hippo opens its mouth super wide and keeps its eyes, ears and nose on top of its head.
An interactive animal lesson for kids ages 2-6, with questions to answer, counting, actions to copy, quick checks and a quiz at the end.
facts: White rhino: two horns on the rostrum, one in front of the other; composed of keratin (not true horns); grow continually throughout life; upper lip broad, flat, specialized to help secure grass; poor eyesight; good sense of smell; second-largest land mammal, only surpassed in size by elephant; skin very thick with deep folds (SDZWA Library fact sheet 'White Rhinoceros', Physical Characteristics, ielc.libguides.com/sdzg/factsheets/whiterhino/characteristics, read Nov 17 2026).

Giraffe: long prehensile tongue, 50 cm (20 in); ossicones bony in adults, soft and cartilaginous in calves, present at birth; individuals can be recognized by their unique markings (SDZWA Library fact sheet 'Giraffe', Physical Characteristics, ielc.libguides.com/sdzg/factsheets/giraffes/characteristics, read Nov 17 2026).

Giraffe: long, prehensile, sticky tongue enables a giraffe to feed on hard-to-reach leaves; strip leaves between lower teeth and hardened upper dental pad; consume 34-75 kg (75-165 lbs) of browse per day; food quickly swallowed, later regurgitated and chewed more thoroughly ('chewing cud'); must spread forelegs wide or kneel to drink (SDZWA Library fact sheet 'Giraffe', Diet & Feeding, ielc.libguides.com/sdzg/factsheets/giraffes/diet, read Nov 17 2026).

Hippo: jaws hinged far to the back, allowing an enormous gape of 150 degrees (humans have only 45); canines and incisors enormously enlarged and continuously growing; male canines can grow to 50 cm (1.5 ft); incisors used for digging; eyes slightly periscoped and aligned on top of head along with ears and nostrils; nostrils close before submersion; ears fold into a recessed area to close underwater (SDZWA Library fact sheet 'Hippopotamus', Physical Characteristics, ielc.libguides.com/sdzg/factsheets/hippopotamus/characteristics, read Nov 17 2026).

segments.name: hello
lines: Hello, friends! I am Milo the bluebird.
Today we are learning about amazing animal heads!
Horns, tongues and teeth. Who has what?
Three animal friends will show us. Count them with me. One, two, three!
Are you ready? Let's go!

segments.name: rhino

lines.t: Who has two horns on its nose, one in front of the other?
Is it the rhino? Or is it the cow?

lines: It is the rhino!
Here is the fun fact. A rhino has two horns. A big one in front, and a smaller one behind it.
Let's count the horns. One, two!

lines.t: Do a rhino's horns ever stop growing? Hmm.

lines: No! A rhino's horns keep growing, all its life. They are made of something called keratin.
Look at those two horns!
close:rhino
A rhino has a wide, flat top lip. It helps the rhino hold the grass it eats.
Munch, munch, munch! A big rhino eats lots and lots of grass.
A rhino cannot see very well. But it has a great sense of smell! Sniff, sniff.
And a rhino is big! On land, only the elephant is bigger.
Say it with me. A rhino has two horns!
close:host
Can you make rhino horns? Put one finger on your nose, and one finger just above it!
Now sniff like a rhino. Sniff, sniff, sniff!

lines.t: Quick check! How many horns does this rhino have? Two? Or ten?

lines: Two! One, two. Great job!

short.title: How Many Horns Does a Rhino Have? Rhino Facts

segments.name: giraffe

lines.t: Who has a long tongue, for grabbing leaves up high?
Is it the giraffe? Or is it the pig?

lines: It is the giraffe!
Here is the fun fact. A giraffe's tongue is about twenty inches long!
Twenty inches! A giraffe's tongue is long, and sticky too.

lines.t: How does a giraffe pull the leaves off a branch? Hmm.

lines: It holds the branch with its long tongue, then strips off the leaves, with its bottom teeth and a hard pad on top!
Look how high a giraffe can reach!
close:giraffe
A giraffe eats lots of leaves and twigs. Up to one hundred sixty-five pounds, in one day!
Later, it brings the food back up, and chews it again. That is called chewing its cud! Chew, chew.
On top of its head, a giraffe has bumps called ossicones. They look like little horns.
A baby giraffe has them when it is born, and they are soft!
Say it with me. A giraffe has a long tongue!
close:host
Can you stick out your tongue like a giraffe? Reach, reach, for the leaves!
Now chew, chew, chew, like a giraffe chewing its cud.

lines.t: Quick check! Is a giraffe's tongue long? Or short?

lines: Long! About twenty inches long. You remembered!

short.title: How Long Is a Giraffe's Tongue? Giraffe Facts

segments.name: hippo

lines.t: Who can open its mouth really, really wide?
Is it the hippo? Or is it the cow?

lines: It is the hippo!
Here is the fun fact. A hippo can open its mouth super wide. Much, much wider than you can!
Can you open wide like a hippo? Open, open, wide!

lines.t: Do a hippo's big teeth ever stop growing? Hmm.

lines: No! A hippo's big front teeth keep growing, all its life.
Wow, what a big mouth!
close:hippo
A daddy hippo's longest teeth can grow about a foot and a half long!
And a hippo uses its front teeth to dig. Dig, dig, dig!
A hippo's eyes, ears and nose are all on the top of its head.
So it can sit in the water, and still look and listen. When it goes under, its nose closes up tight!
Say it with me. A hippo has a big, wide mouth!
close:host
Open wide like a hippo one more time. Big, big mouth!
Now pinch your nose shut, like a hippo going under the water. Blub, blub!

lines.t: Quick check! Where are a hippo's eyes? On top of its head? Or on its feet?

lines: On top of its head! Peekaboo! Super thinking!

short.title: How Wide Can a Hippo Open Its Mouth? Hippo Facts

segments.name: quiz
lines: Wow! We met three amazing animal heads. Now it is quiz time!
Get ready. Think hard!
quiz: Who has two horns on its nose?
Who grabs leaves with a long, long tongue?
Who can open its mouth super wide?

segments.name: goodbye
lines: You learned so many new things today.
Two horns like a rhino. A long tongue like a giraffe. And a big mouth like a hippo!
Which animal head is your favorite?
Thank you for learning with me. Bye-bye, friends! See you next time!
